name: India Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 + DPDP Rules 2025 (duty map)
disclaimer: Our own plain-English summary of duties for AI usage logs. Not legal advice and not a certification.

dates.date_basis: Rule 1(2)-(4): Rules 1, 2, 17-21 on publication; Rule 4 one year later; Rules 3, 5-16, 22, 23 eighteen months later. Act sections 3-16 are assumed to start with them (check the MeitY commencement notification before relying on it).

sources.what: Rules summary (law firm): Rule 6 one-year logs, Rule 7 72 hours

penalties_note: penalty_max_inr_crore is from the Act's Schedule (s.33(1)): s.8(5) up to 250, s.8(6) up to 200, s.9 up to 200, s.10 up to 150, anything else up to 50.

controls.name: Have a lawful ground (consent or a listed legitimate use) for each AI purpose
evidence: feature list with purpose per feature

controls.name: Give a clear notice before or at consent: data, purpose, how to withdraw, how to complain
Consent is free, specific, informed and as easy to withdraw as to give
Be able to prove notice and consent if challenged
Stay responsible for processing done by AI providers on your behalf
Use a provider (Data Processor) only under a valid contract
evidence: signed DPA or provider terms per provider

controls.name: Keep personal data used for decisions complete, accurate and consistent
evidence: data quality checks on AI inputs

controls.name: Encrypt, mask or tokenise personal data (e.g. strip PII before prompts)
evidence: PII-exposure counts from the PII scan (F-15)

controls.name: Control who can access AI logs and raw prompts
Log, monitor and review access to personal data
Keep backups so processing can continue after a breach or outage
Keep logs and the personal data in them for at least one year (unless another law says otherwise)
Have technical and organisational measures that make the safeguards work
Tell each affected user about a breach without delay
evidence: breach plan that covers AI providers

controls.name: Tell the Data Protection Board at once, then send a detailed report within 72 hours
evidence: breach plan with 72-hour Board report template

controls.name: Erase personal data when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is no longer served
Warn the user at least 48 hours before erasing for inactivity
Publish contact details of a DPO or a person who answers data questions
Run a grievance system and answer within 90 days
Publish how users can ask to access, correct or erase their data
Get verifiable parental consent for children's data; no tracking or targeted ads at children
evidence: age gate or parental consent flow

controls.name: Do not process children's data in a way likely to harm their well-being
Check whether you are a Significant Data Fiduciary; if so, DPO in India, yearly DPIA and audit
Track which countries receive data (provider regions) and follow any Government restriction
evidence: provider region per model in the inventory
